title: tenant-role-propagation-and-audit-orphaning-during-kms-envelope-rotation
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Several private-deployment customers reported transient authorization failures followed by missing audit events during a recent scheduled KMS envelope rotation. Root cause analysis points to a race between the async claim-rewrap worker and the SSO role-propagation path: when a SAML assertion arrived exactly while a tenant KMS envelope rotated, the tenant-claim unwrap code returned a partially-initialized authorization artifact. This artifact was accepted by the RBAC layer (granting short-lived access) but the audit pipeline dropped the event due to a nil metadata field introduced by the race. Symptoms: 1) Intermittent 403s for legitimate users (requests re-evaluated after retry succeeded). 2) Missing audit records for the authorization grant and subsequent access for affected sessions. 3) Reproduction reliably triggered by: a) KMS rotation event, b) concurrent assertion processing within 250ms window, c) tenant-scoped ephemeral grants enabled.

Impact: Affected ~4 customers on Private (VPC) clusters running tenant-envelope-rotation scheduled windows. Customer reports included confusion about why access appeared granted but no audit trail existed. This is a compliance risk (audit gap) and a security risk (brief unexpected grant state). Timeline: - 2026-03-11 02:12 UTC: automated KMS envelope rotation began in cluster us-west-2-priv-3. - 2026-03-11 02:12:05 UTC: customer A reported sporadic 403s. - 2026-03-11 03:00 UTC: on-call escalated to Security and Infra. - 2026-03-12: RCA completed by infra + auth teams; reproducer created.

Root cause: The async rewrap worker used a non-blocking cache invalidation path that allowed a partially-updated envelope descriptor to be returned to the unwrap flow. The unwrap function did not handle the descriptor version mismatch nil-safely, leading to two issues: (1) a transient in-memory grant object missing a binding->tenant_id mapping (causing missing audit tenant metadata), and (2) a window where RBAC evaluated policies using the in-memory grant before the descriptor backfill finalized.

Mitigation performed: - Emergency mitigation deployed (2026-03-12 06:18 UTC): added a conservative lock around envelope descriptor fetch during rotation to prevent concurrent unwraps from seeing partial state. This was pushed as a limited hotfix to the affected Private clusters (us-west-2-priv-3 and eu-central-priv-1) and validated by replaying reproducer. - Short-term config change: extended rotation guard window and throttled assertion ingestion for tenants under rotation to reduce collision probability.

Patch summary: - Fix: make envelope descriptor read atomic and add defensive nil-checks in unwrap to fail closed (reject assertion) rather than produce incomplete grants. - Add additional audit fallback: if tenant metadata is missing on grant emission, emit an explicit audit event referencing the assertion and mark as "audit-incomplete" so compliance teams can trace. - Add unit + integration tests that simulate concurrent rotation+unwrap to validate correctness.

Verification: Post-deploy checks executed: 1) Reproducer run (1000 concurrent SAML assertions during rotation) — 0 missing audit events and no 403 regressions. 2) Canary customers validated (Customer A & B): no further 403 reports. 3) Observability: no increase in error rate in auth path; audit event count reconciles with expected grant emissions in the 24h window after patch.

Next steps / follow-ups: 1) Postmortem (owner: Miguel) due by 2026-03-20; include timeline & remediation. 2) Remove temporary ingestion throttle after 2 weeks if metrics remain stable. 3) Long-term: redesign rewrap worker to use versioned descriptors + STM-style compare-and-swap to eliminate locking (epic: ENG-641000). 4) Notify Compliance teams and affected customers; provide signed attestation of audit restoration.
